article.title: Your Googlebook won’t lose some of its best AI features even after your free AI Pro plan ends
article.summary: TL;DR Magic Pointer and Rambler won’t require a Google AI Pro subscription on Googlebooks. The new laptops include free 12 months of AI Pro, but the built-in features are separate from that perk. That means those headline AI features should keep working after the free year ends. Google is putting AI front and center with its first wave of Googlebooks , from Magic Pointer, which turns the humble cursor into a Gemini tool, to Rambler, which cleans up your rambling voice notes. There’s just one potential catch: every Googlebook also comes with a free year of Google AI Pro, which raises an obvious question about what happens to those headline AI features once the freebie runs out. article.title: CRA全面適用倒數15個月，西班牙Applus+帶來CRA協調標準與公告機構最新一線進展，呼籲臺灣企業及早展開產品分類與合規準備
article.summary: 歐盟《網路韌性法》（Cyber Resilience Act，CRA）將於2027年12月11日全面適用，對產品銷往歐洲的臺灣業者而言，如何因應CRA已成為迫切課題。目前正申請成為CRA公告機構（NB）的西班牙業者Applus+ Laboratories，近日在臺說明CRA在歐洲的最新進展與第一線觀察。

article.title: Googlebook laptops are already selling out just days after pre-orders opened
article.summary: TL;DR Google’s US online store has already sold out of its available Googlebook pre-order stock just days after orders opened. Acer, Dell, and Lenovo Googlebooks are all unavailable there, suggesting stronger-than-expected demand or limited initial inventory. Best Buy still has Googlebooks available to pre-order ahead of their October 4 release. Google gave US shoppers barely enough time to decide whether its shiny new Googlebooks deserved a spot in their backpacks before making that decision a little harder. Pre-orders only opened on September 21 , but just a few days later, Google’s own online store appears to have burned through its available inventory. article.summary: 雲端服務暨資安業者Akamai周四（9/24）宣布，擴大與Anthropic的合作，後者將在未來7年採購總值116億美元的雲端運算服務，以滿足持續成長的CPU工作負載需求。雙方合作規模未來還可能增加至約200億美元，Anthropic並取得認購Akamai最高約5%股權的權利。

article.title: When AI Agents Cross Chip Design Silos
article.summary: Key Takeaways: Chip design is moving toward specialized AI agents working together. Orchestration, integration, and guardrails are becoming critical. Human engineers still play a central role in guiding and validating designs and processes. AI agents are becoming smarter, more capable, and increasingly optimized for specific tasks, creating new opportunities to use smaller language models instead of relying on large language models for every task. This shift has broad implications for the semiconductor industry, from the actual design and manufacturing of chips to how those chips function under different workloads. article.title: Autonomy Levels For Design Agents: L1 To L5 Explained
article.summary: Agentic AI plays an important role in chip and system design, but not every “ agentic ” capability has the same degree of autonomy. In practice, autonomy is not binary. It is a progression from AI that optimizes bounded engineering tasks to systems that understand natural language, reason through design problems, and orchestrate multi-step workflows, each representing a different degree of autonomy. That difference matters. When design teams compare autonomy, the useful question is not simply whether a system is “agentic.” It is what the system can decide, what scope it owns, how its work is validated, when it asks for help, and who remains accountable for fallback and final signoff.
